newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish opposition more popular than govt-poll.
newsitem.headline: Swedish opposition more popular than govt-poll.

text.p: Popularity for Sweden's minority Social Democrats government has fallen to its lowest level in six years with the opposition conservative party ranking higher in the latest opinion poll published on Friday.

A survey of 1,000 Swedes in February by Swedish daily Dagens Nyheter an pollster Temo showed support for the ruling Social Democrats has fallen to 27 percent from 31 percent, the lowest level since April 1991.
The opposition party, the Moderates, gained popularity, winning 31.5 percent of support in the poll compared to 28.5 percent at the time of the last poll in December.
The newspaper said the last time the Moderates had more support than the Social Democrats was in January 1996 when a replacement for retiring prime minister Ingvar Carlsson had not been named.
However, then difference between the two parties was only 1.5 percentage points whereas the February poll showed a gap of 4.5 percentage points.
However Dagens Nyheter said the poll results were rather volatile because of a high percentage of voters who said they were unsure about who they would vote for.
Since the poll, the Social Democrats have announced an agreement with the Centre and Left parties in parliament to start phasing out Sweden's nuclear industry in line with a 1980 referendum.
The government said it would close one reactor at Barseback nuclear plant on the southern tip of Sweden by July 1998 -- three months before the next general election.
A second nuclear reactor out of the country's existing 12 would be closed by July 2001.
In the latest poll 18.5 percent of respondees were uncertain compared to 15.5 percent in the December poll.

In the poll the Left party won 14 percent of support against 13 percent last poll, the Greens 8.5 percent (9.5 percent), the Centre party received 7.0 percent (6.5 percent) of support, the Liberals 6.0 percent (5.5 percent) and Christian Democrats 4.5 percent (4.5 percent).
